`git ls-files -v` shows `H` = cached/normal (not assume-unchanged, which would be lowercase h). Yet git status shows clean. Weird. Maybe the index already contains the modified content? Possibly there is a git filter? Or maybe the repo's .git is a symlink to elsewhere and the tool writes... no.

Wait, maybe the working tree was modified and the index got updated by some background process? Unlikely.

Let me check `git diff --no-index` between HEAD version and working file. Or `git show HEAD:internal/shell/shell.go | grep len`.
